text:
elliot: Hey team, first day! Bootstrapping on a company Win11 laptop. Using WSL2 Ubuntu. Hitting weird failures when asdf tries to download plugin tarballs (TLS handshake / certificate unknown). Also node installs with asdf-nodejs complain about gpg keys. Any WSL folks run through this with corp networking? :wave:

matt: welcome Elliot! We had a similar setup. Two common paths: 1) corp CA not trusted inside WSL, 2) proxy intercepts TLS and breaks GPG key retrieval. On Windows I add the corp CA to the Windows store and then export it into WSL.

rachel: For the CA in WSL I do: ```powershell
# run in PowerShell as admin
certutil -addstore -f "Root" "C:\Users\rachel\downloads\corp-root.crt"
# then in WSL
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp && sudo cp /mnt/c/Users/rachel/downloads/corp-root.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp/corp-root.crt && sudo update-ca-certificates
```
That fixed curl/git TLS failures for me.

elliot: ah nice. We authenticate to the proxy via PAC file on the VPN. How do you route WSL traffic through the local proxy?

matt: Two options: 1) run a local proxy on Windows (e.g., Fiddler or cntlm) and forward WSL to 127.0.0.1:port, 2) set WSL to use Windows' networking with `sudo nano /etc/resolv.conf` changes sometimes. I prefer using tinyproxy on Windows and then export HTTP_PROXY inside WSL.

toni: +1 for cntlm if the corp proxy needs NTLM. In WSL I run cntlm on Windows and connect via `export HTTP_PROXY=http://172.17.224.1:3128` where that IP is the Windows host from WSL (check `cat /etc/resolv.conf` for nameserver).

elliot: got it. How about the asdf/nodejs gpg key problem? I see errors like "gpg: Can't check signature: No public key" when asdf-nodejs downloads release tarball.

rachel: asdf-nodejs uses nodesource release signing sometimes. The steps I follow: ```bash
# install required gpg keys
curl -sL https://github.com/nodejs/node/raw/main/README.md | grep -A2 "PGP" || true
# better: use the script the plugin recommends
bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring
# ensure gpg is installed in WSL: sudo apt install -y gpg
```
If the curl is failing because of proxy CA, fix the certs first, then run the import script.

matt: also make sure curl/gnupg uses the same trust store. On WSL the system trust store is what `gpg` reads unless you configured a custom gnupg home.

elliot: thanks. One more: Visual Studio Code Remote - WSL terminal doesn't pick up my exported HTTP_PROXY from ~/.bashrc. Any tips to persist envs in the VSCode remote terminal?

toni: VSCode Remote launches a login and non-login shell depending on settings. Put your exports in both `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`, or better: create `~/.wslenv` on Windows and set envs there so WSL inherits them. Example in PowerShell profile: `setx WSLENV "HTTP_PROXY/p;HTTPS_PROXY/p"` then `wsl -u $USER` will see them. Alternatively enable "Remote > WSL: Use Shell Configuration File" in VSCode settings.

rachel: Another robust pattern: use direnv + a gitignored `~/.local.env` with tokens and proxies for dev work. Then VSCode respects direnv if you install the extension. We also keep `eval "$(asdf init -)"` at top of shell rc so shims work for code actions.

elliot: good call. Any advice for installing tooling on Windows side (scoop vs chocolatey) so asdf and node tooling cooperate?

matt: scoop is lightweight. I install cntlm, 1Password CLI, and git-credential-manager-core via scoop. Example: `scoop install cntlm 1password-cli git-credential-manager-core`. For Homebrew parity on mac, I prefer scoop but chocolatey is fine too.

toni: For git creds on Windows we rely on GCM and SSO. If GCM fails behind proxy: set `GCM_HTTP_PROXY` and `GCM_HTTPS_PROXY` env vars in Windows env config (System Properties > Env Vars) so GUI prompts can reach identity provider.

elliot: last: how do you keep secrets out of dotfiles? I use 1Password app but sometimes the CLI is easier in scripts.

rachel: store secrets in 1Password and pull at login via a small script in `~/.profile` that runs `eval $(op signin --output=raw)` only if interactive. We keep a `~/.secrets.env` in .gitignore and load it with direnv: `.envrc` contains `source_env ~/.secrets.env`. Make sure your repo has a hook preventing `git add` of that file (pre-commit or gitignore rules).

matt: also add a README in your dotfiles repo explaining how to rehydrate secrets (op commands) so a new hire can follow steps.

devops-bot: onboarding: WSL proxy & CA KB updated: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboarding/wsl-proxy-ca ; created ticket INF-412 to add Windows CA push script to infra repo.

elliot: this is great. I'll try the CA import + cntlm route and report back. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
